chapters.why-you-stay: Gap Wood doesn't quit things. You see potential, you see a direction, and you'd rather build than walk away. In a situationship that instinct can keep you planting in soil that never agreed to be a garden. You tell yourself it's growing slowly, that they need time, that you'll know more next month. Sometimes that's true. Often you're staying because leaving would feel like admitting a project failed. Ask yourself plainly: am I here because this feels good now, or because I've already invested so much? Those are very different reasons, and only one of them is about joy.
chapters.what-you-want: You probably know exactly what you want. You just haven't said it, because for Gap Wood saying it out loud means committing to the outcome. Try anyway, privately first. Write one sentence that starts with I want a relationship where, and finish it honestly. Exclusive? Plans beyond next weekend? Being introduced to their friends? Tall trees like clarity. Not knowing where something is heading is genuinely uncomfortable for you, and that discomfort is information. It's telling you that casual may not be what you signed up for, even if you said it was at the start.
chapters.mixed-signals: When signals are mixed, you tend to grab the most hopeful one and build a plan on top of it. A good date becomes evidence of a shared future. Gap Wood reads intention into action and assumes other people move as purposefully as you do. Many don't. A warm night may simply mean they had a warm night. The fix isn't becoming cynical. It's to stop interpreting and start asking. You're good at direct questions in every other part of your life, at work, with family, with friends. You can be good at them here too.
chapters.the-talk: Your version of the talk should be simple, calm, and early in the evening, not after drinks. Gap Wood is persuasive, so the risk is turning it into a pitch for why you two should be together. Don't sell. State. Something like: I like you, and I'm looking for something more defined. What are you looking for? Then stop talking. Truly stop. Let their answer be their answer, without arguing with it or offering a revised proposal. You're not negotiating a contract. You're finding out where another person stands, which is a different and much shorter conversation.
chapters.your-line: Your line is direction. Gap Wood can tolerate slow, but not nowhere. Decide now what you won't keep accepting: maybe being someone's secret, or plans that always shift at the last minute, or months with no definition at all. Write it down and keep it somewhere you'll see it. When you reach that line, you don't need a dramatic exit, only a calm, clear sentence: this isn't working for me. Respecting your line isn't a threat or an ultimatum. It's self-respect, and it's the same quality that makes people trust you everywhere else.
chapters.either-way: Whatever they say, you'll be okay, and you'll know more than you know now. If they want more, wonderful, build it slowly and together. If they don't, you've saved yourself months of growing toward a wall. Gap Wood recovers by redirecting energy, so give yourself a short, real pause first, then put that drive into something that grows back: a goal, a friendship, a fresh start. Clarity costs one slightly awkward conversation. Uncertainty costs a great deal more, paid out slowly in checked phones and second-guessed evenings. You're far better at new beginnings than you give yourself credit for.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You see so much potential in them, Gap. That's lovely.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Potential isn't a relationship. It's a pitch deck.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: It's okay to want something defined.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Then define it. You plan everything else down to the minute.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Ask, then really listen to the answer.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: No selling. No rebuttals. Ask once. Listen once.

chapters.why-you-stay: Eul Wood is the vine, and vines wrap around whatever is nearby. In a situationship you adapt to their rhythm: when they text, when they're free, what they're ready for. You're so good at making things easy that you can stay a long time without noticing you're always the one adjusting. You stay because connection matters to you, and some connection feels better than none. That's human. But ask yourself one gentle question: do I feel more secure since this started, or less? Your honest answer tells you more than any of their texts ever could.
chapters.what-you-want: You might honestly not know what you want, because you've been tuned to what they want for a while. Eul Wood is excellent at reading the room and slower at reading itself. So try this: imagine they offered you anything at all. What would you ask for? A title, consistency, being invited to things, a plan every week? Notice what comes up first, before you edit it down to something reasonable. That first answer is your want. It's allowed to be bigger than what you currently have, and it's allowed to be said out loud.
chapters.mixed-signals: When signals are mixed, you bend to fit them. They're distant, so you give space. They're warm, so you lean in. Eul Wood tends to read their signals as instructions for your own behaviour. The trouble is that your mood and your choices end up depending entirely on theirs. Try noticing your own signal instead. How do you feel after you see them? Lighter and settled, or anxious and checking your phone? That feeling is far clearer than anything they're sending, and it belongs completely to you. Start a quiet note on your phone and log that feeling after each meeting. After three or four entries, the pattern usually speaks for itself.
chapters.the-talk: Your talk can be gentle. That's your strength. But it needs one clear sentence in the middle, or you'll soften it into nothing. Try: I've really liked this, and I'd like to know if we're building toward something. Then add what you want, without apologising for wanting it. Eul Wood loves to offer an escape hatch at the end, the little no pressure though. Skip the escape hatch this time. Let it be a real question that deserves a real answer, and give them the silence they need to give you one.
chapters.your-line: Your line is being chosen. Eul Wood will put up with a lot of inconvenience, but you need to feel like a priority, not a backup plan for a quiet Thursday. Decide what that means in practice: plans made ahead of time, being introduced to people who matter to them, effort to see you that doesn't always come from your side. If that's consistently missing, that's your line. Stepping back doesn't make you dramatic or needy. It makes you someone who knows what shape fits your life, and keeps growing toward it.
chapters.either-way: Either way, you grow. If they want more, lovely, and this time make sure the adapting goes in both directions from the start. If they don't, you get your energy back to wind around things that hold you properly: friends, work, your own plans, maybe a new person who's actually ready. Eul Wood rebounds faster than anyone expects. You look delicate and you are incredibly hard to flatten. Give yourself a few soft days, then reach for the light again. You always find it. And next time, say what you want on the first or second date. It filters fast, and the right person finds it refreshing.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You make everything so easy for them, Eul.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Maybe too easy. When did they last adjust anything for you?

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Your want is allowed to be bigger than this.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And drop the 'no pressure though!' Some pressure. A little.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Notice how you feel after you see them.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Lighter, or glued to your phone? That's your answer.

chapters.why-you-stay: Byeong Fire is the sun, and you love the fun parts: the spark, the late calls, the inside jokes nobody else gets. A situationship can be all highlights and no responsibility, and honestly that's enjoyable for a while. You stay because when it's good, it's really good. But suns need warmth back too. If you've noticed you're giving more energy than you're getting, the fun can start to feel like a performance you're putting on twice a week. Ask yourself: if the fun nights stopped tomorrow, what would actually be left between you?
chapters.what-you-want: You know what you want, and you've probably already joked about it. Byeong Fire tends to say the true thing as a joke so it doesn't land too heavily. Haha, so are we dating or what. Try saying it without the haha. You want to be seen and celebrated, chosen in public and not only enjoyed in private. You want someone who's proud to stand next to your light. That's a completely reasonable thing to want, and you're allowed to want it now rather than at some vague point in the future.
chapters.mixed-signals: When signals are mixed, you probably turn up the warmth: more plans, more energy, more charm, as if clarity were a prize you could win. Byeong Fire tries to shine brighter. It rarely works, because clarity isn't something you earn by performing. It's something they either offer or don't. Instead of increasing your output, try matching theirs for a week. Not as a game or a test. Just to see the real level of effort in this thing when you're not the one carrying all of it on your back.
chapters.the-talk: Your talk will be warm and honest, which is great. The risk is making it big. Byeong Fire can turn a simple question into a speech with three acts and a callback. Keep it short, in an ordinary setting, not at a party or in front of friends. Something like: I'm having fun, and I want to know if this is going somewhere. I'd like it to. What about you? Then let there be silence. Silence is not a fire you need to put out with more words. Let them fill it.
chapters.your-line: Your line is being hidden. Byeong Fire cannot live in the shadows. If you're kept away from their friends, left off their life when you'd like to be part of it, or only ever seen late at night, notice it and name it to yourself. Decide where your line is. When it's crossed, step back without a scene, and without a long explanation post. Your light deserves someone who's openly glad to stand next to it in daylight, in front of the people they love. Notice, too, how often you've made excuses for them to friends. That habit is usually the first sign your line has already moved.
chapters.either-way: Either way, you keep your light. If they want more, wonderful, and let them show it with effort, not only words. If not, you'll be sad, honestly sad, and then you'll be out with friends and laughing far sooner than you expect. Byeong Fire is wonderfully resilient. Just don't sprint to the next spark before you understand why this one didn't catch. One quiet evening of thinking it through will save you from repeating the same lovely, exhausting pattern with someone new. Write three lines about what you learned, then go dancing. Both parts matter, in that order.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: When it's good, it's so good. I get it, Byeong.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And when it's not, you just shine harder. Exhausting.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Say what you want without the joke.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Drop the 'haha'. It's doing a lot of heavy lifting.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You deserve someone proud to be seen with you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Daylight test. Do you only exist to them after 10pm?

chapters.why-you-stay: Jeong Fire is the candle, and when you connect, you connect deeply. Even an undefined thing feels intimate to you, because you bring your whole attention to it. You stay because the moments feel so real: the late talks, the small details they remember, the rare feeling of being understood. The question is whether that intimacy runs in both directions, or whether you're doing most of the feeling and quietly calling it us. Your depth is a gift. Make sure it's being received, not just enjoyed from a comfortable distance.
chapters.what-you-want: You want to be special to them, in a clear and steady way. Jeong Fire doesn't do half-attachments well, and you probably already feel more than you've admitted to anyone, including yourself. Write it down honestly: what would make you feel safe here? Consistent contact, knowing you're the only one, a simple name for what this is? Owning that want isn't needy. It's accurate. A candle needs a still room to burn well, and wanting stillness is not too much to ask of someone you're close to. Say it to yourself first, in a full sentence, so it sounds familiar when you say it to them.
chapters.mixed-signals: Mixed signals are your weak spot. Jeong Fire reads every detail and builds meaning from it. A late reply becomes a whole story, a heart emoji becomes a different one, a full stop becomes a tragedy. Your intuition is often right, but in uncertainty it works overtime and runs out of facts. Try one rule: one interpretation per day, maximum. Then go and do something else with your hands. And notice this: if a person's messages need this much decoding, the message itself is unclear, and that is information too.
chapters.the-talk: Your talk should be calm and in person if you can manage it, at a time when you're rested rather than wound up. Jeong Fire has more courage than people realise, and you're good with honest, intimate words. Say what you feel, briefly: I've gotten attached, and I'd like to know where you are. Then let them answer without filling the silence with reassurance or a quick it's okay if not. You don't need to protect them from your feelings. They're allowed to hold them for a moment. Breathe, keep your hands busy with a cup of tea, and trust that your voice will hold steady enough.
chapters.your-line: Your line is consistency. Jeong Fire can't relax in hot and cold. Decide in advance what counts as too much uncertainty for you: days without contact, plans that keep vanishing, feeling anxious more often than happy. When you hit that line, you step back to protect your flame. That isn't punishment, and it isn't a test to see if they chase you. It's maintenance. A candle in a draughty room either gets moved or goes out, and you get to choose the first option. Write the line down on a calm day, so the anxious version of you at midnight can't quietly rewrite it.
chapters.either-way: Either way, you'll feel it deeply, and you'll be okay. If they want more, beautiful, build it slowly and keep talking honestly as you go. If not, the candle doesn't go out just because one person walked past it. Give yourself quiet, gentle days, time with people who already love you, and some patience. Your capacity for closeness is still fully there, waiting for someone who wants all of it, the depth, the attention, the moods, and treats that as the best part. Light something warm, call someone who knows you well, and let that be enough for one evening.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You bring so much depth to this, Jeong.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And they bring... a heart emoji every four days.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Wanting to feel special isn't needy.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: One interpretation per day. You're on number nine.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Say how you feel. Calmly. You're braver than you think.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: If it needs this much decoding, that's the message.

chapters.why-you-stay: Mu Earth is the mountain: patient, steady, slow to move. In a situationship you wait. You assume things will settle into a shape if you just keep being reliable. At first you may not even mind the low pressure, since it asks nothing dramatic of you. You stay because leaving would require a decision you haven't fully made, and because you're loyal even to things without a name. Ask yourself one practical question: am I waiting for something specific to happen, or am I just waiting because waiting is what I do?
chapters.what-you-want: You want stability, someone you can actually count on. Mu Earth rarely says that out loud, because you'd rather show it than ask for it. You show up, you keep your word, you remember things. But being reliable yourself doesn't automatically make the other person reliable back. Name your want plainly: consistent plans, exclusivity, someone who shows up when it matters and not only when it's convenient. If that isn't happening, more patience from you is not the fix. It's simply more of the same. Wanting it doesn't make you demanding. It makes you clear about the foundation you'd build on.
chapters.mixed-signals: When signals are mixed, you tend to ignore them and hold your course. Mu Earth is very good at not reacting, which keeps you calm and steady. It also means you could sit for months in something that never actually moved. Instead of waiting for one clear signal, look at the pattern over time. Has anything grown, deepened, or become more defined since the first month? Are you meeting their friends, making plans further ahead? Mountains notice erosion slowly. Check the landscape honestly. If the honest answer is nothing has changed, then the stillness is the signal, and you can stop waiting for a louder one.
chapters.the-talk: Your talk can be straightforward, almost practical, and that suits you well. Pick a calm moment, maybe a walk where you're side by side. Say: I like what we have, and I'd like it to be more defined. Where are you at? Mu Earth's risk is saying it so neutrally that they don't realise it matters to you at all. So add one honest sentence on top: this matters to me. Then listen properly, without deciding in advance what their answer means or how you'll react. Afterward, give yourself a day before deciding anything. You process best slowly, and that's allowed.
chapters.your-line: Your line is being taken for granted. Mountains are reliable, and people lean on them without thinking about it. If you're always the available one, the one who adjusts plans, the one with no real say in what this is, notice that pattern. Decide what effort you need in return, in concrete terms. When it's missing week after week, step away calmly and without drama. Mountains don't chase. They don't have to. The right people climb toward them on purpose. Write down two or three concrete examples of effort you'd expect. If you can't remember the last time you saw one, that tells you plenty about where things stand.
chapters.either-way: Either way, you'll stand. If they want more, it will be built on something solid, because you are solid. If not, you'll take some time, probably more than you show anyone, and then you'll move forward with your usual quiet strength. Let one friend know how you're actually doing, in honest words rather than I'm fine. Even mountains need company sometimes. You've been the steady thing for other people for so long. Let someone be steady for you for a week. Then shift one small thing in your week, a new route or a new class, so your life feels like it's moving too.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You've been so patient and steady, Mu.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Patient, or just not deciding? Be honest.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Wanting stability is reasonable.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Then say 'this matters to me'. Out loud. With your mouth.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Look at the pattern, not one good night.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Has anything moved since month one? Check the map.

chapters.why-you-stay: Gi Earth is the garden, and you nurture whatever is in front of you. In a situationship you probably give a lot: you listen, you help, you remember things, you make every evening cosy. You stay because caring is your way of loving, and because part of you hopes that enough care will eventually turn this into something real. Ask yourself, gently but honestly: is this growing because of us, or only because of me? If you stopped watering it for two weeks, would anything still be standing? That question can sting a little. Answer it anyway, quietly, just for yourself.
chapters.what-you-want: You want to be taken care of too. Gi Earth often forgets to put that on the list at all. Think practically for a moment: what would care from them actually look like? Checking in on a hard day, making the plan for once, showing up when you're stressed without being asked. You're allowed to want a partner who tends your garden as well as their own. It's not asking too much. It's asking for even, which is the minimum for anything you'd call a relationship. Write down three small acts of care you'd love to receive. Specifics make it easier to notice when they're missing.
chapters.mixed-signals: When signals are mixed, you worry, and then you try harder. More effort, more help, more thoughtful little gestures. Gi Earth hopes that care will create clarity. Usually it creates comfort for the other person instead, and comfortable people rarely feel any urgency to define things. Pause your effort for a short while and simply see what they do on their own. Their unprompted effort, the plans they make and the check-ins they start, is a far more honest signal than how warmly they respond to yours. Two weeks is usually enough to see the real shape of things without your hands holding it up.
chapters.the-talk: Your talk should be practical and kind. Gi Earth is good at sensible, grounded conversations. Try: I've really enjoyed this, and I need to know if we're moving toward something real. Resist the strong urge to soften it with but no worries if not. There are worries, and that's fine. Your needs aren't a bother or an imposition. Let them be real in the room. Then give them space to answer honestly, even if the honest answer isn't the one you were hoping for. Make it a calm daytime conversation, not a late-night one where you're tired and more likely to back down.
chapters.your-line: Your line is one-sided effort. Decide what minimum mutual care looks like for you, written down in plain terms. If you keep doing all the planning, all the checking in, all the emotional work while they simply turn up, that's your line crossed. Stepping back doesn't mean abandoning them or being unkind. It means leaving a garden that never fed you, so you have the energy to plant one that will. You can be gentle and still be finished. Notice how you feel on Sunday evenings. If it's drained rather than full, your body already knows where the line is.
chapters.either-way: Either way, your care isn't wasted. It's who you are, and it goes with you. If they want more, make sure it's balanced from the very first week. If not, redirect all that warmth toward yourself and toward the people who already return it. Gi Earth heals well with routine, good food, and friends who notice you. You'll grow something new, and this time it will be properly tended from both sides, which is what you deserved all along. Start with something small and selfish this week: a meal you love, an evening that belongs to nobody else.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You make everything so warm for them, Gi.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Unpaid caretaking for someone who won't commit. Love that for you.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You're allowed to want care back.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And stop saying 'no worries if not'. There are worries.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Pause the effort and see what they do.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Their effort without prompting. That's the only data that counts.

chapters.why-you-stay: Gyeong Metal is the blade, direct and loyal. Honestly, situationships aren't your natural habitat, because you like things clear and labelled. So if you're in one, something about this person got past your defences. You might be staying out of pride, not wanting to be the one who cares more first. Or you said casual at the beginning, and you keep your word even when it no longer fits. Check whether that early promise still matches who you are now, or whether you're just being loyal to an old sentence.
chapters.what-you-want: You want clarity and loyalty, plainly. Gyeong Metal knows this about itself. You might have avoided saying it because asking feels like showing weakness, like handing over a point. It isn't. A direct question is your superpower, and you use it brilliantly everywhere else in your life. You want to know where you stand, and you want to stand somewhere solid. That's a completely fair want. Not asking doesn't make you cooler. It just keeps you in a grey zone you actively dislike. Say it the way you'd say anything else important to you: simply, calmly, and once, without decoration.
chapters.mixed-signals: Mixed signals frustrate you more than most people. Gyeong Metal sees in black and white, and grey can feel almost like disrespect. You might respond by going cold, quietly testing them, or delivering an ultimatum far too early. Try something in between those options: a calm, direct question. Not a test. Not a verdict. Just: where are we? You'll learn more from one honest question than from three weeks of silent observation, and you'll keep your dignity fully intact. If you notice yourself drafting an ultimatum in your head, take that as a cue to ask the question instead.
chapters.the-talk: You'll handle the talk well, as long as it stays a conversation and not a cross-examination. Gyeong Metal can sound sharper than intended, especially when nervous. Soften the delivery, not the content. I like you. I want something clear. What do you want? Then let them think for a moment. A slow answer isn't automatically a bad answer, and people who are put on the spot often say less than they mean. Give the silence a little room before you draw any conclusions. Keep your arms uncrossed and your tone level. Your words are already clear, so let your body language be easy.
chapters.your-line: Your line is honesty. Gyeong Metal can handle hard truths, but not being kept vague or misled. Decide clearly what you won't accept: dodging the question again and again, hidden other people, promises that never match actions. When it's crossed, you step away cleanly. You don't need a speech or a final word. You don't need to prove they were wrong. Just leave with your head up. Walking away calmly says everything a speech would say, with better posture. Decide your line on a calm day, before you're angry, so it reflects your values rather than your mood.
chapters.either-way: Either way, you come out clear, which is what you wanted all along. If they want more, you'll build it with your usual fierce loyalty. If not, you'll cut cleanly and probably feel it later, quietly, when you least expect it. Let yourself feel it when it arrives. Strength and sadness can share a room without either one winning. Then go back to the people who already know exactly where they stand with you, because you told them. Go to the gym, call your oldest friend, and let both of those count as taking care of yourself.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You care about honesty more than anything, Gyeong.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Then why are you in a situationship? That's your opposite.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Asking where you stand isn't weakness.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Ask once. Calmly. No interrogation lamp.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Soften the delivery, keep the message.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: If they dodge the question twice, that's the answer.

chapters.why-you-stay: Sin Metal is the jewel, refined and selective. You don't fall easily, so if you're in a situationship, this person impressed you. You might stay because you like the idea of them, or because asking for more feels like exposing yourself in an unflattering light. You'd rather be elegantly casual than visibly invested. Ask yourself honestly: is the casualness real, or is it a very beautiful cover for wanting something you're scared to ask for? Only you know, and you probably already do. Write the answer in one honest line, just for yourself. Nobody else needs to see it.
chapters.what-you-want: You want to be treasured. Seen in detail. Chosen with intention, not by default. Sin Metal has high standards, and that includes how you're treated by the people you let close. You may have lowered them temporarily to keep this light and easy. Write down what you'd want if you weren't worried about looking like too much. That list is your real standard, and it's not too high. It's simply specific, which is what good taste looks like when it's applied to love. Keep the list somewhere private and read it before your next date with them. See how it compares to what's actually happening.
chapters.mixed-signals: When signals are mixed, you analyse them with precision and then pretend you didn't notice anything. Sin Metal stays composed on the outside while quietly scoring every exchange on the inside. That costs a surprising amount of energy. Instead of grading their behaviour in silence, ask one simple question out loud. Your perception is genuinely sharp, but a clear answer from them will always beat a perfect guess from you, and it lets you put the scorecard away. One plain question, asked kindly, is more elegant than months of silent judging anyway.
chapters.the-talk: Your talk will be graceful. The risk is that it's so polished it doesn't sound like it matters to you. Let a little real feeling show through. I like you, and I want more than this. Is that something you want too? Don't over-rehearse it in the mirror. A slightly imperfect version, with a pause or a nervous laugh, carries far more truth than a flawless one. People trust the cracks in a voice more than the shine on a sentence. Choose a quiet place you like, somewhere beautiful helps you, and keep it short enough that the feeling stays in it.
chapters.your-line: Your line is carelessness. Sin Metal can't stay where it's treated as optional. Plans cancelled without care, details forgotten, effort that only ever goes one way. Decide what isn't acceptable for you, specifically. When it happens repeatedly, not once on a bad week but as a pattern, step away with grace. You don't have to fight to be valued or prove your worth in an argument. The right person notices it without being shown a list. Write down two or three things that would tell you you're being treated as optional. Then trust yourself when you see them.
chapters.either-way: Either way, your worth stays exactly where it was. If they want more, wonderful, let them show it with care and attention to detail. If not, it's their loss of something genuinely rare. Give yourself time and beauty, a quiet weekend, something lovely just for you, and then return to your high standards without apology. They aren't the problem here. They're a filter, and filters are supposed to keep some things out. Yours is working. Buy the flowers. Wear the good coat. Remember that your taste brought you here and it will bring you somewhere better.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You don't fall easily, Sin. They must have impressed you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And now you're pretending to be casual. Elegantly. Badly.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Your standards are not too high.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You're grading every text in silence. Just ask the question.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Let a little real feeling show.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Don't rehearse it into a press release.

chapters.why-you-stay: Im Water is the ocean, and you love your freedom. Honestly, a situationship can suit you for a while. No pressure, plenty of space, nobody asking where you are on a Saturday. You might stay because it's easy, or because defining it would feel like signing up for a cage. But check yourself here. Are you genuinely happy with how undefined it is, or are you avoiding the question because answering it would mean staying in one harbour for longer than you're used to? Both answers are allowed. Just make sure it's the real one.
chapters.what-you-want: You might want something deeper than you're admitting. Im Water often thinks it wants freedom, when what it really wants is freedom with someone. What would good commitment look like for you, in your own terms? Space to roam, with a home to come back to? Separate adventures and shared Sundays? Define your version without borrowing anyone else's template. It doesn't have to look like your friends' relationships or anything on a screen. It only has to fit you and one other person. Write it as three short lines. If you can't, that's a sign to sit with the question a little longer before you ask them anything.
chapters.mixed-signals: Here's the twist: you might be the one sending mixed signals. Im Water flows, warm and present one week, distant and busy the next, and doesn't always notice the change from the outside. And when they're unclear, you tend to drift rather than ask. Check both sides of this honestly. What am I communicating with my behaviour, and what am I avoiding asking with my words? Sometimes the fog you're trying to see through is partly your own weather. A simple fix: tell them when you're going quiet for a few days. It costs one message and saves a lot of guessing.
chapters.the-talk: Your talk can be relaxed and open, which suits you. Maybe on a walk or a long drive, where nobody has to stare across a table. The risk is keeping it so light that nothing actually gets decided. Say what you want, even if it's a bit unconventional: I like this, I want to keep seeing you, and I want to know if it's just us. Be specific about the parts that matter. Freedom works much better with clear terms than with vague vibes. And listen to their answer as carefully as you'd study a map before a big trip.
chapters.your-line: Your line is control. Im Water won't stay anywhere it's boxed in or monitored. But notice your other line too, the one you talk about less: being someone's option. Even an ocean wants to matter to the shore. Decide what you need on both sides, room to breathe and real importance. When those aren't there, let the tide carry you somewhere else, honestly and with a clear goodbye, rather than simply drifting out of contact and hoping they get the message. Both lines can exist at once. Wanting space and wanting to matter isn't a contradiction. It's just being honest.
chapters.either-way: Either way, you'll flow on. If they want more, great, build a version with room to breathe for both of you. If not, you'll explore, travel, meet people and recover quickly. Just make sure you actually feel it before you set sail again. Oceans have real depths, and you're allowed to visit yours. Give the feeling one honest evening of your attention. Then go wherever you want to go, lighter, and a little clearer about what you're looking for next time. Maybe write it down somewhere you'll find it again on your next trip.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You love your freedom, Im. That's real.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You also love not answering hard questions. Also real.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Maybe you want freedom with someone.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Warm one week, gone the next. You might be the mixed signal.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Define your own version of commitment.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Freedom with terms. Write them down. On land.

chapters.why-you-stay: Gye Water is the rain, intuitive and gentle. You feel deeply and quietly, and a situationship lets you keep those feelings unspoken, which can feel safe. You might stay because you sense something real between you, a connection that doesn't need words. Or because asking would feel far too exposing. Ask yourself softly: is the mystery here romantic, or is it just unclear? Romantic mystery makes you feel more alive. Unclear makes you feel more anxious. You can tell the difference if you're honest. Put your hand on your chest, ask the question, and notice what comes up first.
chapters.what-you-want: You want emotional closeness, to be understood without having to explain every single thing. Gye Water hopes that other people will simply intuit what it needs. They won't, not fully, not even the kind ones. So write your want down plainly: I want to know where I stand. I want to feel safe. I want us to be a real thing with a name. Seeing it in words makes it real, and it makes it much easier to say out loud when the moment comes. Read it back to yourself a few times until it stops sounding scary and starts sounding simply true.
chapters.mixed-signals: When signals are mixed, you absorb them. Their mood quietly becomes your mood. Gye Water can go from happy to anxious on the strength of one short reply. Your intuition is a real and useful tool, but in fog everything looks bigger and closer than it is. Try writing down facts only: when they reached out, what they did, what they actually said. Leave out the guesses about what it meant. Fog clears remarkably fast once it's on paper. Read the list the next morning, in daylight, when everything feels a little more manageable.
chapters.the-talk: Your talk can be soft, but it has to contain actual words. Gye Water tends to hint and hope. Try a direct, gentle sentence: I've been feeling more for you, and I'd like to know where we are. You could write it down first to find the right phrasing. Then say it rather than text it, if you can, so your voice carries what the words can't. They deserve to hear the real you, and you deserve to see their face when they answer. If your voice shakes, let it. Shaking and honest is far better than steady and hidden.
chapters.your-line: Your line is emotional uncertainty that leaves you drained. If you're more anxious than happy, more confused than close, more alone than together, that is your line. Decide what you need to feel steady, and when it's missing, step back gently. You don't need a big confrontation or a dramatic exit. Rain simply moves on when the season changes, and nobody accuses the rain of being unfair. You're allowed to change seasons too. Write your line in your journal on a calm, clear day, so you can read it back when the fog rolls in. Then trust the version of you who wrote it.
chapters.either-way: Either way, you'll be okay, and you'll be clearer than you are right now. If they want more, keep using your words, every week, even when it feels exposing. If not, let yourself feel it fully, cry if you need to, and then let it pass through. You deserve someone who wants to understand you, and who finally gets the chance to, because you spoke up instead of waiting to be guessed. That's a win, whatever their answer was. Then go and stand in actual rain for a minute. It helps more than it should.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You feel so much, Gye, even when you don't say it.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Exactly. You don't say it. They're not mind readers.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Writing your feelings down first is a great idea.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Then say them out loud. Hints are not a language.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Facts on paper clear the fog.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: One reply shouldn't control your whole mood. Phone down.

by_element_balance.too_much_wood: Too much Wood means you push for growth and definition. In a situationship you might rush clarity, or picture a whole future before the other person has caught up to the present. Your drive is a good thing. Just give them room to answer at their own pace once you've asked. Ask once, clearly, then step back and let the answer come. Balance with a little Metal: clear boundaries, finished business, knowing when something needs pruning rather than more growth.
by_element_balance.missing_wood: Missing Wood means starting things, including the talk, feels hard. You might let an undefined situation drift on and on simply because initiating anything feels heavy. Build momentum in small steps: decide what you want, write it down, choose a day to ask. Spend time outdoors and around green things. You don't need to grow everything at once. You only need one honest question, asked once, out loud.
by_element_balance.too_much_fire: Too much Fire means big feelings, fast. In a situationship you might swing between excitement and frustration in the same evening, and want answers right now. Slow your pace a little. Pick a calm moment for the talk, not a heated one. Cool down with water: rest, quiet nights in, a walk before sending any big message. Your passion is attractive. Just don't let it make your decisions at midnight.
by_element_balance.missing_fire: Missing Fire means expressing feelings and being seen can feel hard. You might keep this situationship low-key so that nobody, including you, has to admit it matters. Turn the light up a little. Let your feelings show in small ways. Be visible in your own life too: plans, friends, sunlight, music. The more you shine for yourself, the easier the honest question becomes when you finally ask it.
by_element_balance.too_much_earth: Too much Earth means you wait, stay steady, and stay put, sometimes for too long. In a situationship you may tolerate a lack of definition because change feels disruptive and messy. Bring in a bit of movement: pick a day by which you'll have the talk, and keep it. Let some Wood in, growth and fresh starts. Stable doesn't have to mean stuck, and patient doesn't have to mean silent.
by_element_balance.missing_earth: Missing Earth means stability is hard to find, and an undefined relationship can make you feel even more unsteady than usual. Ground yourself first: routines, regular meals, a dependable circle of friends. Then have the talk from a steady place, not a shaky one. You'll think more clearly and ask more clearly when your own ground is solid under your feet, whatever the answer turns out to be.
by_element_balance.too_much_metal: Too much Metal means you want clarity and might cut too fast to get it. In a situationship you may issue ultimatums or go cold the moment things feel vague. Your boundaries are strong, which is good. Soften the delivery: ask with curiosity first, decide second. Water helps here: rest, reflection, letting a feeling be felt before you act on it.
by_element_balance.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are hard. In a situationship you may accept less than you want and keep telling yourself it's fine. Practise clear edges: decide your line and write it down somewhere you'll see it. Say no to plans that don't work for you. White and silver, decluttering, finishing things all support you. A boundary isn't harsh. It's honesty about what you need.
by_element_balance.too_much_water: Too much Water means overthinking and very deep feeling. In a situationship you might analyse every message and drown in what-ifs that never happen. Your intuition is valuable, but it needs a shore to land on. Earth helps: routines, physical activity, friends who ground you. Put a limit on the analysis. Ask the question instead of guessing the answer.
by_element_balance.missing_water: Missing Water means reflection and rest get skipped. You might keep the situationship busy and fun so you never have to stop and think about what it actually is. Make space for quiet: a journal, a slow evening, a moment alone to ask yourself what you really want here. Clarity starts inside you before it's ever spoken to them, and it's worth the quiet.
